result.title: Manga Page Parser: Comprehensive Visual Parsing through Local Story Understanding
result.summary: Understanding manga requires connecting who appears and who speaks with the events, character states, and relationships that unfold across panels. We study manga visual parsing through local story understanding: analyzing each double-page spread independently to capture and organize its story information in a reusable structured representation. We propose MangaParser, an agentic reading framework that jointly performs character clustering, speaker diarization, and speaker-to-character binding within a shared multimodal conversation, without additional training or fine-tuning. The agent uses structured story memory to guide character and speaker identification, inspecting relevant image regions when uncertain and refining its predictions and story records together as evidence accumulates. Quantitative evaluations show that our parser substantially outperforms manga-specific models across multiple backbones. Parsing examples illustrate how a unified representation links the character and speaker predictions with narrative content and supporting evidence. We further test reusability through story question answering using outputs generated before the questions are provided. The results confirm output reusability, offering a foundation for manga translation, content retrieval, and question answering.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 MangaParser，一个无需训练的 agentic 阅读框架，在同一多模态对话中联合完成角色聚类、说话人分离与说话人—角色绑定，并借助结构化故事记忆指导识别、在不确定时局部重看图像区域，最后用故事问答检验输出的可复用性。
AI.relevance_reason: 漫画解析本身不涉及 latent 推理，但其「结构化记忆作为可复用中间状态」与「不确定时回看局部证据」的做法，可能为 LVR 的外部推理状态表示与证据筛选、停止决策提供概念参照，值得核查。
